question: A 28-year-old pregnant female presents for a prenatal check-up at 20 weeks gestation, which includes routine screening ultrasound. Fetal ultrasound demonstrates bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys. Her pregnancy has been complicated by persistent oligohydramnios. The child requires significant pulmonary support upon delivery. Which of the following clinical findings is most likely present in this child as a result of these abnormalities?
analysis: The scenario describes a fetus with bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys and persistent oligohydramnios. Oligohydramnios, a condition characterized by low amniotic fluid, can lead to Potter sequence, which includes pulmonary hypoplasia (underdeveloped lungs) due to the compression of the fetal chest. This condition necessitates significant pulmonary support after birth. Among the options provided, clubbed feet (positional deformities of the feet) are also a common feature in Potter sequence due to the oligohydramnios and resultant compression of the fetus in utero.
